title: Weapons and Tactics Instructor (II/III) (LtCol to 2ndLt) and (CWO5 to WO) NMOS (6002, 6004, 6302), DC AVN
raw_text:
4. MOS 6077, Weapons and Tactics Instructor (II/III) (LtCol to 2ndLt) and
(CWO5 to WO) NMOS (6002, 6004, 6302), DC AVN

    a. Summary. Weapons and Tactics Instructors train aviation maintenance
professionals in the execution of various tasks that are encompassed within a
wide spectrum of aviation maintenance and logistics matters. They will (1)
Assist their respective unit commanders in conducting a professional Marine
Corps Aviation Weapons and Tactics Training Program (WTTP) which includes
specific individual MOS training and collective operational unit training;
(2) Act as aviation logistics managers and planners with enhanced planning
skills and insight into integrating all aviation assets to promote mission
success; (3) Coordinate and conduct appropriate supplementary courses
applicable to their particular community; (4) Ensure all training conducted
under their supervision is properly documented and adheres to established
safety procedures; (5) Submit appropriate information, including exercise/
deployment reports, to assist MAWTS-1 in updating tactics and instruction.

       b.   Prerequisites.   Must possess Primary MOSs 6002, 6004, or 6302.

    c. Requirements. Complete the Marine Aviation Weapons and Tactics
Squadron One Advanced Aircraft Maintenance Officer Course (M14FDG1).

       d.   Duties

        (1) Serves as the aviation logistics and maintenance management
standardization representative to the organizational and intermediate level
units on all issues relating to training standards, training development,
training management, and evaluation.

        (2) Provides training and readiness (T&R) guidance and serves as the
official signature authority for T&R signoffs within their assigned scope.




                                         1-242                        Enclosure (1)
 1135                                                           NAVMC 1200.1L



        (3) Reviews, investigates, introduces, and evaluates emerging
standardization techniques and ensures the broadest dissemination to the
fleet.

        (4) Coordinates and facilitates professional development
opportunities and classroom training for maintenance professionals ensuring
standardization IAW the most current fleet practices.

        (5) Serves as a maintenance operations planning liaison providing
expertise to units planning large scale detachments and deployments.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Teachers and Instructors, All Other, Except Substitute Teachers, 25-3097.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.




                                         1-243                   Enclosure (1)
 1136                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L

Weapons and Tactics Instructors train aviation maintenance professionals in the execution of various tasks that are encompassed within a wide spectrum of aviation maintenance and logistics matters.
Oversee training programs.

They will (1) Assist their respective unit commanders in conducting a professional Marine Corps Aviation Weapons and Tactics Training Program (WTTP) which includes specific individual MOS training and collective operational unit training.
Organize flight plans or traffic management plans to prepare for planes about to enter assigned airspace.
(2) Act as aviation logistics managers and planners with enhanced planning skills and insight into integrating all aviation assets to promote mission success.
Teach community courses and speak to local groups and organizations.
(3) Coordinate and conduct appropriate supplementary courses applicable to their particular community.
Train new employees in areas such as safety procedures or equipment operation.
(4) Ensure all training conducted under their supervision is properly documented and adheres to established safety procedures.
Prepare and submit required reports related to instruction.
(5) Submit appropriate information, including exercise/ deployment reports, to assist MAWTS-1 in updating tactics and instruction.
Establish and implement operational standards and procedures for the departments supervised.

d. Duties (1) Serves as the aviation logistics and maintenance management standardization representative to the organizational and intermediate level units on all issues relating to training standards, training development, training management, and evaluation.
Monitor industry standards, trends, or practices to identify developments in logistics planning or execution.
(3) Reviews, investigates, introduces, and evaluates emerging standardization techniques and ensures the broadest dissemination to the fleet.
Review, develop, or prepare maintenance standards.
(4) Coordinates and facilitates professional development opportunities and classroom training for maintenance professionals ensuring standardization IAW the most current fleet practices.
Plan, organize, and execute logistics support activities, such as maintenance planning, repair analysis, and test equipment recommendations.
(5) Serves as a maintenance operations planning liaison providing expertise to units planning large scale detachments and deployments.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
